research_mode: official HSE and GOV.UK primary guidance only; gas, asbestos, smoke/carbon-monoxide alarm and residential fire-safety regulatory and methodology gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Smoke and carbon-monoxide regulation scope
verified_claims: The guidance applies in England to relevant private and social rented homes, subject to listed exclusions.
limitations: Regulatory scope cannot be assigned without tenancy-specific evidence.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Smoke alarm per occupied storey
verified_claims: Relevant landlords must ensure at least one smoke alarm is equipped on each storey containing a room used as living accommodation.
limitations: The rule does not specify that one alarm is adequate for every layout or risk profile.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Carbon-monoxide alarm combustion-appliance duty
verified_claims: A carbon-monoxide alarm is required in each living-accommodation room containing a fixed combustion appliance, excluding gas cookers.
limitations: Appliance presence and room use must be established for the specific property.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Faulty alarm repair or replacement
verified_claims: Landlords must repair or replace prescribed smoke and carbon-monoxide alarms after being informed and finding that they are faulty.
limitations: A tenant report alone does not establish the technical fault or completion of repair.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Alarm-regulation local-authority enforcement
verified_claims: Local housing authorities enforce the alarm requirements.
limitations: Enforcement responsibility does not mean action has occurred at a named property.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Alarm-regulation penalty ceiling
verified_claims: A local authority can impose a civil penalty of up to £5,000 where a landlord fails to comply with a remedial notice.
limitations: The statutory ceiling is not evidence that a breach or penalty exists.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Alarm placement legal-detail boundary
verified_claims: The regulations do not stipulate the exact position of smoke or carbon-monoxide alarms.
limitations: Absence of a prescribed position does not remove the need for effective installation.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Alarm manufacturer-instruction gate
verified_claims: Landlords should follow individual manufacturer instructions when installing alarms.
limitations: Manufacturer guidance must be matched to the actual alarm model.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: General smoke-alarm placement guidance
verified_claims: The guidance generally recommends smoke alarms on the ceiling in circulation spaces such as halls or landings.
limitations: This general recommendation is not a substitute for model-specific instructions or risk assessment.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: General carbon-monoxide alarm placement guidance
verified_claims: The guidance generally recommends carbon-monoxide alarms at head height and approximately one to three metres from a potential source.
limitations: The general distance should not override manufacturer-specific requirements.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Alarm battery and landlord repair boundary
verified_claims: Tenants are advised to replace batteries during a tenancy, while landlords remain responsible for repairing or replacing faulty alarms.
limitations: Responsibility can depend on whether a battery change resolves the fault.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Accessible alarm alerting
verified_claims: Specialist alarms using vibration or flashing lights may be required for residents who are deaf or hard of hearing.
limitations: A resident's accessibility needs must not be inferred from property data.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Heat detector non-substitution
verified_claims: Heat detectors are not a replacement for smoke alarms under the guidance.
limitations: A heat detector may still form part of a wider fire-safety system.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Alarm working-order check at tenancy start
verified_claims: Landlords must check prescribed alarms are in proper working order on the day a new tenancy begins.
limitations: The duty does not establish that a documented test occurred for a specific tenancy.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: Alarm-regulation tenancy exclusions
verified_claims: The guidance lists exclusions including landlord-shared accommodation, long leases, student halls, hotels, refuges, care homes, hospitals, hospices and certain low-cost ownership or healthcare accommodation.
limitations: An exclusion must be verified from the legal tenancy and use, not inferred from building type.
